notes:
Summary: Nebula Context Labs builds a knowledge layer for regulated enterprise customers (legal and compliance teams). They currently run a hybrid search stack: dense vectors in FAISS + a lightweight cross-encoder reranker. Seeking to migrate embeddings and reranker to higher-throughput models to reduce cost-per-query while maintaining or improving relevance. Key constraints: indexing scale (~300M docs, 20-40B tokens of context), tail latency SLO 150-250ms P50 for semantic queries, P95 < 800ms for reranked results, and strict data residency (US, some EU for subsidiaries).

Evals focus: customer wants an eval-first migration. They provided ~5k labeled queries and a set of targeted hard-query prompts (legal citations, short queries with long-answer requirements). Concern: potential quality regressions when moving from their tuned SBERT->cross-encoder to a quantized embedding model + light reranker. Ask: show regression delta on business metrics (safety/precision for legal citations, recall of precedent docs).

Operational asks: private deployment in VPC with customer KMS, audit logs forwarded to Splunk, retention controls, SSO via SAML, SOC2 compliance proof. They want canary/A-B capability (route 5/20/50% traffic) and automated rollback if eval metrics drop beyond thresholds. Also interested in Redwood Optimize for batching suggestions and quantization profiles to hit cost targets.

Quoted from engineering director: "If we see more than a 3% drop in legal-citation precision we can't proceed — downstream teams rely on exact matches."

POC plan (agreed): ingest 25M doc subset -> build new embedding index with float16/8-bit quantization -> run offline evals vs baseline -> start 5% canary for two weeks with live telemetry and daily eval snapshots -> expand if no regression. Redwood to provide canary routing config, eval hooks, and rollback policy template.

Open items: final pricing for Private + Dedicated hybrid, SLA for P95, encryption-at-rest proof, legal review timeline (expected 6 weeks), and sample eval dashboard for stakeholders.

Next meet: 2026-03-16 technical working group (Redwood SE, Nebula Eng, Legal Ops).
